theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Why does a Level 3 electrician inspect the team's work before the government electrical inspector comes?
options: To find and fix faults before the official visit
To make the official government inspection unnecessary
To give the team a reason to slow down the job
To check that the client has paid the deposit

questions.stem: What is an 'acceptance criterion' in an inspection?
options: The name of the person who did the work
The stated limit or standard the work must meet
The date on which the inspection is booked
The tool that is used to take the reading

questions.stem: The specification says all socket circuits are wired in 2.5 mm² cable, but you find one run in 1.5 mm². What is the right decision?
options: Accept it, because the circuit still works
Accept it, because the cable is new and neat
Record it as not meeting the specification
Change the drawing so that it says 1.5 mm²

questions.stem: Where should an inspector look first to find what a finished installation must meet?

What the team did on the last job
The supplier's latest price list
The specification and drawings

questions.stem: The inspection plan for a rewire marks some stages 'HP'. What does a hold point mean for the team?
options: A stage where work stops until it is inspected and signed off
A place on site where all the tools are locked away each night
A mark on the drawing where a cable is held by a clip

questions.stem: Why should conduit and boxes set into a block wall be inspected before the plasterer starts?

The plasterer needs the report to be paid

questions.stem: You are writing an inspection checklist for a shop fit-out. Which line is written best?
options: Wiring looks good and tidy
Check that everything is fine
Each breaker labelled to match the chart

questions.stem: Before an inspection, you see that the insulation tester is past its calibration due date. What is the right action?
options: Use it, but take every reading twice
Use it on this job and report it later
Move a newer label from another meter
Withdraw it; use an in-date meter

questions.stem: Why is a voltage indicator checked on a proving unit both before and after a circuit is proved dead?
options: To show it worked, so the 'dead' reading can be trusted
To charge the indicator's battery ready for use
To set the indicator to the right voltage range for the circuit
To record the supply voltage on the test sheet

questions.stem: Which instrument would you use to check that a conduit's outside diameter is 20 mm, to a fraction of a millimetre?
options: Steel tape measure
Vernier caliper
Feeler gauge
Digital multimeter

questions.stem: A delivery of circuit breakers arrives with no maker's markings, and they feel very light. What should you do?
options: Fit them on a small job first to try them
Put them on the shelf with the good stock
Quarantine them and report them

questions.stem: When you inspect a drum of cable on delivery, which marking shows it is the size you ordered?
options: The colour painted on the drum
The supplier's phone number
The weight on the delivery note
The size printed on the sheath

questions.stem: What is a quarantine area in the store used for?
options: Keeping failed or doubtful items away from use
Keeping tools that are waiting to be sharpened
Storing the materials for the next week's job
Holding items that have passed and are ready

questions.stem: A batch of 200 identical socket outlets arrives. The quality plan asks for a sample check. What does this mean?
options: Every outlet in the batch is opened and tested
A set number are picked at random and checked
Only the outlets on top of the box are checked
The supplier checks them and you just sign

questions.stem: In a sample check, 2 of the 10 outlets you open have loose terminal screws. What is the best next step?
options: Accept the batch, since most are good
Fix the two and accept the rest unseen
Check more or all, and tell the supplier
Throw the whole batch away straight away

questions.stem: In a distribution board you see bare copper showing outside a breaker terminal. Why is this a defect?
options: It makes the board harder to label
It uses more copper than is needed
It lowers the voltage reaching the socket outlets
It can be touched or cause a short circuit

questions.stem: Which of these findings on a cable run should be recorded as a defect?
options: Clips spaced wider than the specification allows
Cable run straight and level along the ceiling
Sheath carried fully into the accessory box
Cable kept well clear of the hot water pipe in the roof

questions.stem: An outlet on an open verandah wall is the same type as the indoor ones. What should the inspector check?
options: That it matches the colour of the wall
That its IP rating suits wet, outdoor use
That it is at least 2 m from the door
That it uses longer screws than the others

questions.stem: Why does the inspector check that the cable glands on a metal enclosure are tight?
options: So the enclosure can be painted later
So the enclosure looks like the others
So the cable is held and its sheath protected
So the enclosure is heavier and harder to move

questions.stem: Inside a socket outlet you find the earth conductor under the same terminal as the neutral. What should you do?
options: Leave it, as both go back to the board
Tape over it so the client cannot see it
Note it for the next yearly inspection
Record a defect and have it corrected

questions.stem: Before any dead test is done as part of an inspection, what must be done to the circuit?
options: Isolate, lock off, tag and prove it dead
Switch on all of its loads to warm the cable up
Pull the breaker out of the board
Ask the client to stay out of the room

questions.stem: An insulation resistance result is within the limit but much lower than on similar circuits. What should a Level 3 inspector do?
options: Pass it, since it meets the limit
Look for the cause and note it
Retest it at a higher voltage
Change the limit on the sheet

questions.stem: Why are test readings compared with the values expected for that cable's length and size?
options: To show that the meter battery is still good
To work out how much the cable cost to buy
To spot a reading that looks wrong for the circuit
To decide which breaker to buy for the next job

questions.stem: A meter's accuracy is ±2% of the reading. It reads 0.50 Ω. Between which values could the true value lie?
Two inspectors measure the same protective conductor and get different low-resistance readings. What should be checked first?
options: Whether both nulled their test leads
Whether the cable is the right colour
Whether it rained the day before
Whether both meters are the same age

questions.stem: Why should inspection results be written on the record at the moment they are taken?
options: So the record can be thrown away sooner
So readings are not forgotten or mixed up
So the inspector can leave the site earlier
So the client can sign before the testing

questions.stem: Which details make an inspection record traceable later?
options: The inspector's favourite meter
The weather on the day of the check
Who inspected, when, and with which instrument
The price paid for each item checked

questions.stem: You wrote a wrong reading on the inspection sheet. What is the accepted way to correct it?
options: Paint over it with correction fluid
Tear out the page and start again
Rub it out and write the new value
Strike it through once, rewrite and initial

questions.stem: What is a 'non-conformance'?
options: Work or material that does not meet a requirement
A meeting where the team agrees the plan for the week
A change that the client asks for in writing
A job that is finished ahead of its programme

questions.stem: Which action closes out a non-conformance properly?
options: The defect is fixed, and nobody is told
The defect is fixed, re-inspected and signed off
The defect is written down and the job closed
The worker who caused it is moved to another job

questions.stem: An inspector finds a defect that could give someone an electric shock. When should it be reported?
options: In the weekly summary at the end of the week
When the team starts on the next job
At once, with the circuit kept isolated
Only if the client asks about it

questions.stem: Why is a defect labelled at the place it was found, as well as written in the report?
options: So it looks as though more work was done
So the label can be used again on another job
So the client is charged for the label as well
So nobody uses or covers it before it is fixed

questions.stem: Who should normally receive the inspection report on a team's finished work?
options: The supervisor or person in charge of the job
Only the worker whose work was checked
The firm that supplied the materials
Any member of the public who asks to read a copy

questions.stem: Which line is best written in an inspection report?
options: Board looked bad
Circuit 4 breaker is 32 A; chart says 20 A
Some breakers are the wrong size
Many small problems were found

questions.stem: Why should an inspection report say which parts were NOT inspected?
options: To make the report longer and look thorough
To blame another trade for the missing parts
So nobody thinks those parts were checked
So the inspector can charge for another visit

questions.stem: You need to take the cover off a distribution board to inspect its terminations. What must come first?
options: Tell the client you will be very quick
Wear gloves and do it carefully while live
Switch off only the one circuit you will look at
Isolate the board, lock off and prove it dead

questions.stem: Which hazards should an inspector plan for before going into a roof space to inspect cable runs?
options: Heat, poor light and stepping between joists
Cool breeze and too much fresh air
Noise from the client's radio below
Bright light that makes notes hard to read

questions.stem: What is a go/no-go gauge used for?
options: Measuring an exact size to two decimal places
Checking quickly if an item is within limits
Testing whether a circuit is live or dead
Marking where a hole is to be drilled

questions.stem: Which is the best example of an 'in-process' inspection?
options: Checking cable as it arrives at the store
Checking the whole job at handover
Checking terminations as each board is wired
Checking the client's bill after the job

questions.stem: A specification says a light fitting is mounted 2.40 m above the floor, ±50 mm. Which height passes?
Why does the inspector check the circuit chart in a board against the circuits that are actually there?
options: So anyone isolating a circuit switches off the right one
So the board looks neat when the door is opened
So the client can see what each circuit cost
So the breakers can be moved around later

questions.stem: Why should the inspector check that a cable or breaker carries a recognised approval mark?
options: It shows that it was the cheapest one
It shows it was tested to a known standard
It means it never needs inspecting again
It shows which shop sold the item

questions.stem: You find the same defect, loose neutral screws, on three jobs done by one team. What is the best Level 3 action?
options: Fix them quietly each time you find them
Stop that team from working straight away
Report the pattern so its cause can be fixed
Ignore it, since the screws were tightened

questions.stem: Why might an inspector use a torque screwdriver on terminal screws?
options: To strip the insulation off the conductor end
To test the voltage at the terminal
To loosen terminals that have rusted
To check they meet the maker's tightness

questions.stem: At the Centre, after inspection and dead testing are complete and every defect is fixed, who energises the installation?
options: The instructor, after checking the work
The trainee who wired the circuits
Any member of the group who says they are ready

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What word describes checking an instrument against a known reference to confirm that it reads correctly?
What do the letters NCR stand for on an inspection form?
A conduit length must be 3.00 m ± 10 mm. What is the shortest length that passes, in metres?
What is the name for the list of small defects that must still be fixed before handover?
What two letters, followed by two digits, show how well an enclosure keeps out dust and water?
A sample of 20 outlets is checked and 2 fail. What percentage failed?
What screwdriver, set to a fixed value, is used to tighten or check terminal screws to the maker's figure?
In which unit is insulation resistance normally recorded on a test sheet?
Name the small device that gives a known voltage so that a voltage indicator can be checked before and after use.
What word describes being able to follow an item or a result back to its source and records?
What kind of inspection is done using the eyes and hands only, without instruments?
A specification gives a clip spacing of 300 mm. How many 300 mm spaces are there along a 2.4 m straight cable run?

A tester is calibrated every 12 months. It was last calibrated in March 2026. In which month and year is it next due?

essays.stem: You lead a small team wiring a two-room office. Explain how you would plan the inspections from the delivery of materials to handover.
essays.modelAnswer: I would start from the specification and drawings and list what must be checked and the limit for each. I would plan an inspection of materials on delivery: sizes, ratings, approval marks and damage. I would set hold points: conduit and boxes inspected before the walls are plastered, cable runs and supports before ceilings close, and board terminations before covers go on. At the end I would plan a full visual inspection, then the dead tests in the right order, done after safe isolation. I would choose the instruments, check they are in calibration and book them. I would prepare a checklist and a record sheet for each stage, say who inspects and who signs, and agree with my supervisor how defects will be recorded, labelled and re-inspected. The plan ends with the report, the snag list and the handover pack.
markingPoints: Uses the specification and drawings to set what is checked and the limits
Inspects incoming materials
Sets hold points before work is covered up
Plans final visual inspection and dead tests after safe isolation, with calibrated instruments
Prepares checklists and records, and says who inspects, signs and follows up defects

essays.stem: Describe how you would inspect a delivery of cable, breakers and accessories before they are given out to the team, and what you would do with items that fail.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would check the delivery note against the purchase order: item, size, rating and quantity. I would count the items and look for damage to boxes, drums and cable sheaths. On the cable I would read the size, number of cores and type printed on the sheath. On breakers I would check the rating, number of poles, type and the maker's and approval markings, and look for items that look or feel fake. For a large batch of accessories I would open a random sample and check terminals and covers. I would record the results on a goods-in inspection sheet. Items that fail or are in doubt are tagged, moved to the quarantine area and reported to my supervisor and the purchaser, so the supplier can replace them. Only items that pass are put into stock.
markingPoints: Checks delivery note against the order: item, size, rating, quantity
Looks for damage and reads markings on cable and breakers
Checks approval marks and watches for fake items; samples large batches
Records the results
Tags and quarantines failed items, reports them, and only issues items that pass

essays.stem: Describe what you would look for in a visual inspection of a finished distribution board and its circuits, and say why each check matters.
essays.modelAnswer: With the board safely isolated and proved dead, I would check that the board is fixed firmly and its cover and blanks are fitted, so no live part can be touched. I would check each breaker's rating against the circuit chart and the cable size, because a breaker too large will not protect the cable. I would look for bare copper outside terminals, damaged insulation and loose or doubled conductors, which can cause shock, heat or a short circuit. I would check that earth and neutral conductors are on the correct bars and in circuit order. I would check that cables enter through glands or grommets with no sharp edges, that the board is labelled, and that the circuit chart is complete and correct, so the right circuit can be isolated in future. I would also look for signs of heat, such as discoloured insulation.
markingPoints: Done with the board safely isolated and proved dead
Cover, blanks and fixing so no live part can be touched
Breaker ratings match the chart and cable sizes
Terminations: no bare copper, damage, loose or doubled conductors; earth and neutral bars in order
Cable entries protected, labels and circuit chart complete, signs of heat checked

essays.stem: Explain the steps of safe isolation you would follow before opening accessories and boards for inspection, and why each step is needed.
essays.modelAnswer: First I identify the right circuit from the chart and the drawings, so I isolate the correct one. I switch it off at the breaker or isolator. I lock it off with my own padlock and keep the key, so nobody can switch it back on. I fix a tag with my name, the date and the reason, so others know why it is off. I check my voltage indicator on a proving unit to show it works. I then test between all the conductors at the point of work, line to neutral, line to earth and neutral to earth, to prove the circuit dead. Then I check the indicator on the proving unit again, to show it did not fail during the test. Only then do I open the accessory or board. Work is never done live.
markingPoints: Identifies the correct circuit
Switches off, locks off and keeps the key
Fixes a tag with name, date and reason
Checks the indicator before, tests all conductors, checks it again after
States that work is never done live

essays.stem: Explain why inspection instruments must be calibrated and checked, and describe what you would do if you found that a meter used last week was out of calibration.
essays.modelAnswer: An instrument can drift and read wrongly over time, or after a knock. If it reads wrongly, a faulty circuit could be passed as safe, or a good circuit failed. Calibration against a known reference, at set intervals, shows the instrument is accurate, and the record gives confidence in every result taken with it. Before each use I also check the leads, the battery, and null the leads for low-resistance readings. If I found a meter out of calibration, I would stop using it at once, tag it 'do not use' and report it. I would find every job where it was used since its last good calibration, and with my supervisor decide which results need retesting with a calibrated instrument. I would record what was found and what was done, and send the meter for calibration or repair.
markingPoints: Instruments drift; wrong readings could pass unsafe work
Calibration at set intervals with records gives confidence
Checks before use: leads, battery, nulling
Stops using and tags the faulty meter, reports it
Traces the jobs since the last good calibration and retests as agreed, and records it

essays.stem: Describe how you would deal with a non-conformance found during inspection, from finding it to closing it out.
essays.modelAnswer: When I find work that does not meet the requirement, I first make it safe: if there is any danger the circuit stays isolated and locked off. I label the item at the place it was found so nobody uses or covers it. I write a non-conformance report saying what was found, where, what requirement it fails and who found it, with a photo if possible. I report it to my supervisor. We agree the fix, who will do it and by when, and whether the cause needs action, for example more training. When the fix is done, I re-inspect it, and retest it dead if needed. If it now passes, I sign it off and close the report. The report is kept with the job records.
markingPoints: Makes it safe first; keeps circuit isolated if dangerous
Labels the item where found
Writes a non-conformance report with the details and reports it
Agrees the fix, who and when, and looks at the cause
Re-inspects, signs off, closes and files the report

essays.stem: Explain what makes a good inspection record and why records must be accurate, complete and kept.
essays.modelAnswer: A good inspection record names the job, the location and the item or circuit checked. It gives the requirement or limit, the actual reading or finding, and whether it passed. It shows who inspected, the date, and the instrument used with its serial number and calibration date. It is written at the time, in pen, clearly, and any mistake is struck through once and initialled, not rubbed out. It is signed. Records must be accurate because people decide whether the installation is safe from them. They must be complete, so nobody thinks a part was checked when it was not. They are kept so the firm can show later what was checked, deal with a complaint or claim, compare readings at the next inspection, and trace a problem back to its cause.
markingPoints: Identifies job, location and item checked
Gives the limit, the actual result and pass or fail
Shows who, when and which instrument
Written at the time, clear, corrections struck through and initialled, signed
Explains why accuracy, completeness and keeping matter

essays.stem: Compare checking every item (100% inspection) with sample inspection. Say when each is the better choice in electrical work.
essays.modelAnswer: In 100% inspection every item is checked. It finds every fault, but it takes more time and costs more. In sample inspection a set number of items are picked at random and checked, and the result is taken to show the quality of the whole batch. It is quicker and cheaper, but a few faulty items may be missed. Sample inspection suits large batches of identical, low-risk items, such as boxes of cable clips, screws or blank plates, from a supplier with a good record. If the sample shows faults, more or all are checked. 100% inspection is better for anything that affects safety, such as every circuit's protective conductor, every board termination and every breaker rating, and for items made one at a time on site. In an installation, all the finished circuits are inspected and tested.
markingPoints: 100% finds all faults but takes more time and cost
Sample: random selection, quicker, may miss some faults
Sample suits large batches of identical low-risk items
Faults in a sample lead to more or full checks
100% for safety items and the finished circuits

essays.stem: The same defect keeps appearing in your team's work. Explain how you would use the inspection results to find and remove the cause.
essays.modelAnswer: I would collect the inspection records and count how often the defect appears, where, on which tasks and who did the work, so I can see the pattern. I would talk with the team without blaming anyone and ask why it happens. I would keep asking why until I reach the real cause: for example the screwdrivers are worn, there is no torque figure in the method, or new members were never shown the correct way. I would agree a fix that removes the cause, such as new tools, a short training session, or adding a check to the checklist. I would tell my supervisor and record the action. Then I would watch the next inspection results to see if the defect has stopped. If it has not, I would look again.
markingPoints: Collects and counts the records to see the pattern
Talks with the team without blame
Finds the root cause by asking why
Agrees and records a fix that removes the cause, and informs the supervisor
Checks later results to confirm it worked

essays.stem: Explain why clear acceptance criteria are needed before inspection begins. Give three examples of acceptance criteria for an electrical installation.
essays.modelAnswer: Acceptance criteria are the limits or standards that decide whether work passes or fails. If they are not clear before inspection starts, two inspectors may judge the same work differently, arguments start, and unsafe work may be passed. Clear criteria come from the specification, the drawings, the maker's instructions and the code the Centre uses. They let the team know the target before they work, and let the inspector give a fair yes or no. Examples: every breaker rating matches the circuit chart and the cable size on the drawing; insulation resistance of each circuit is at or above the minimum value the code the Centre uses gives; switch heights are 1.2 m above the finished floor, plus or minus 20 mm; every enclosure fitted outdoors has the IP rating that the specification asks for.
markingPoints: Defines acceptance criteria as the pass or fail limits
Without them judgements differ and unsafe work may pass
Criteria come from the specification, drawings, maker's instructions and code
Gives three clear, measurable electrical examples

practical1.title: Plan and carry out an inspection of a completed training-board installation
practical1.brief: The assessor gives the group a completed installation on the Centre's training boards (a small board with lighting and socket circuits), its drawings and specification, and a blank inspection plan. The installation is dead and stays dead: the assessor has built in a number of defects. As an inspection team: (1) write an inspection checklist from the specification, with a clear pass limit for each line; (2) carry out and record safe isolation of the training board (switch off, lock off, tag, prove dead with a tester checked on a proving unit before and after); (3) carry out a full visual inspection of the board, cable runs and accessories; (4) carry out continuity checks of the protective conductors with a calibrated low-resistance ohmmeter, nulling the leads first; (5) record every result on the record sheet; (6) label each defect where it is found and write a non-conformance report for each; and (7) write a short inspection report to the assessor, who acts as supervisor. Each member leads one area of the inspection and checks another member's findings. Photograph each stage.
materials: Completed training-board installation with built-in defects, drawings and specification (from the assessor)
Lock-off kit: padlocks, hasps and danger tags for each member
Low-resistance ohmmeter or multifunction tester with a calibration label in date
Torch, inspection mirror, screwdrivers and a torque screwdriver
Blank checklist, record sheets, non-conformance forms and defect labels
Clipboards, pens and a phone or camera for photos
photos: The written checklist with pass limits
The training board locked off and tagged, and the tester being checked on the proving unit
A member inspecting terminations in the board
A continuity test being taken with nulled leads
A defect labelled where it was found
The completed record sheet and non-conformance reports
checklist: Wrote checklist lines that are clear and measurable, taken from the specification
Carried out safe isolation correctly: off, lock, tag, tester checked before and after proving dead
Checked the instrument's calibration date and nulled the leads before use
Found the built-in defects in their area and judged each against the criteria
Recorded each result clearly, at the time, with corrections struck through and initialled
Labelled each defect and wrote a complete non-conformance report
Checked another member's findings and helped write a clear, factual report
safety: The training board stays dead for the whole task; only the instructor may energise anything
Prove dead with a tester that is checked on a proving unit before and after use
Each member fits their own lock and tag and keeps their own key
Use insulated screwdrivers in good condition and keep the work area tidy
Follow the maker's instructions for each instrument and the Centre's rules

practical2.title: Goods-in inspection of a delivery of electrical materials
practical2.brief: The assessor sets up a mock delivery of electrical materials with a purchase order and a delivery note: cable drums or coils, circuit breakers, socket outlets, switches, conduit and fittings. Some items have been made faulty: a wrong cable size, a short count, damaged accessories, a breaker of the wrong rating, an item with no markings, and conduit of the wrong diameter. As a goods-in team: (1) write a goods-in inspection plan, saying which items get a 100% check and which get a sample check, and how many are sampled; (2) check the delivery note against the order; (3) read and record the markings on the cable and breakers; (4) measure conduit diameters and conductor sizes with a vernier caliper; (5) open and check a random sample of accessories; (6) record every result on an inspection sheet; (7) tag and move failed items to a quarantine area; and (8) write a short report to the purchaser listing what passed, what failed and what must be returned. Each member is in charge of one group of items, and the group then swaps to check one another's results. Photograph each stage.
materials: Mock delivery of electrical materials with built-in faults (from the assessor)
Purchase order and delivery note for the delivery
Vernier calipers and a steel tape measure
Inspection sheets, quarantine tags and a marked quarantine area
Clipboards, pens and a phone or camera for photos
photos: The goods-in inspection plan with the sample sizes
The delivery note being checked against the order
Markings being read on the cable and breakers
A conduit or conductor being measured with a vernier caliper
Failed items tagged in the quarantine area
The completed inspection sheet and the report to the purchaser
checklist: Chose sensibly which items get a 100% check and which a sample, and explained why
Checked items, sizes, ratings and quantities against the order
Read markings correctly and spotted the items with missing or wrong markings
Used the vernier caliper correctly and read it accurately
Recorded every result clearly on the inspection sheet
Tagged and quarantined each failed item
Checked another member's results and helped write a clear report
safety: Lift cable drums and boxes safely; get help or use a trolley for heavy items
Watch for sharp edges on cut conduit and damaged boxes; wear gloves when handling them
Keep walkways clear of items while they are being checked
No item is connected to any supply during this task
